tone_statements.citation: Jordan, Dean. 1978. Nafaara tense-aspect in the folk tale. In Joseph E. Grimes (ed.), Papers on discourse, 84-90. Summer Institute of Linguistics Publications in Linguistics and Related Fields 51. Dallas: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
tone_statements.quote: ²Nafaara has the following consonant phonemes: stops p b t d č j k g kp gb, fricatives f v s z š h, laterals l r, nasals m n ny ŋ, and semivowels w y. The vowels are i e ɛ a u o ɔ. All may be lengthened, symbolized by writing them double … There are three tones: high, mid, and low. See Carol Jordan's study of Nafaara phonology for more details. … [p. 86] The fusion of pé 'they' with wè 'future' results in a tone glide. Continuative nà works in the same manner, but is distinct in tone from ná 'past'.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low) stated in a phonology footnote; examples marked with acute, grave and some macrons; fused pronoun+particle forms carry a tone glide. Nothing on downstep or stress.
